claims.text: The initial W38Ta36Cr15V11 material is a magnetron-sputtered nanocrystalline thin film with equiaxed BCC grains and an approximately 70 nm scale.
The initial material was deposited at room temperature and pre-annealed at 1173 K.
Reducing Cr from 15 at.% to about 10 at.% while increasing V from 11 at.% to about 16 at.% will suppress irradiation-induced Cr–V-rich precipitates near 8 dpa.
Increasing V produces enhanced V-dependent chemical short-range order.
The proposed compositional adjustment yields a more homogeneous BCC solid solution.
The proposed compositional adjustment yields a finer grain structure.
The proposed adjustment makes vacancy and self-interstitial mobilities more closely matched.
Increasing V weakens ordering or segregation tendencies among Ta, V, and W.
Weaker ordering or segregation among Ta, V, and W suppresses the tendency of Cr and V to form precipitates.
Higher V increases irradiation-defect recombination by reducing the disparity between self-interstitial and vacancy mobilities.
Increased defect recombination reduces the accumulation of large defect clusters that drive precipitation.
After approximately 8 dpa at 1073 K, the modified alloy will exhibit a marked reduction or elimination of Cr–V-rich precipitates relative to W38Ta36Cr15V11.
The modified alloy will maintain low irradiation-induced hardening.
The modified alloy will retain a nanocrystalline BCC morphology after irradiation.
The proposed composition will not compromise bulk manufacturability.
Unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 develops Cr–V-rich precipitates near 8 dpa at 1073 K.
Unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits significant irradiation-induced hardening near 8 dpa at 1073 K.
Unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 has overall good radiation resistance.
The predicted result is limited to magnetron-sputtered nanocrystalline BCC thin films irradiated up to about 8 dpa at approximately 1073 K.
Transfer of the result to bulk materials or to doses above 20 dpa or temperatures above 1273 K is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome says that low irradiation-induced hardening will be maintained relative to the baseline, whereas the baseline is described as exhibiting significant hardening.

The predicted outcome states that bulk manufacturability will not be compromised, but the boundary and uncertainty fields say that extrapolation to bulk material is uncertain and may face scaling challenges.
